inline.s: Practical Training Materials
Living in Awareness
Its practice has steps by which to enter;
its realization has a truth that is won for oneself.
Perseverance is passion for long-term goals, together with persistence.
Excellence in work comes from diligence, and is ruined by play;
Carve without letting up, and even metal and stone can be engraved.
The three “froms” and the one “great”:
strictly, under hard conditions, and starting from real combat;
great volume of training.
Diligently cultivate discipline, concentration, and wisdom; extinguish greed, anger, and delusion.
[Under hard conditions] Practice only in the “learning zone.” For details see
Ten Thousand Hours of Deliberate Practice Make a Genius
Deliberate practice:

Expert-level performance is trained up gradually, and the key to effective progress lies in finding a series of small tasks and having the trainee complete them in order, so that the goal can be reached. These small tasks must be ones the trainee just cannot yet do, and yet can just manage to learn and master. Completing this kind of practice requires the trainee to concentrate intensely, which makes it entirely different from routine or entertaining practice.

Whether we are learning small life skills such as playing ball, driving, playing an instrument, or cooking, or improving key work abilities such as writing, sales, programming, or design, none of it is possible without a great deal of practice. But we usually have a great misunderstanding about practice: isn’t practice just repetition over and over? No! Mere repetition is only ‘
naive practice
’, and it brings no progress. ‘
Correct practice
’ requires good guidance (teaching yourself is simply being your own guide), goals, and feedback.

inline.s: The goal of awareness in Buddha-recitation is: faith and vows, holding the name, one mind undisturbed, and ensuring rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss beyond doubt. This is something every reciter of the Buddha’s name can attain through diligent effort.

Awareness in Buddha-recitation is based on a focused, continuous, and enduring power of awareness, in order to attain one mind undisturbed in Buddha-recitation. It is therefore divided into two great parts: preliminary practice and Buddha-recitation — the Preliminary Practices section and the Buddha-Recitation section. In the preliminary practices, one cultivates the power of awareness through training in “awareness of movements,” “awareness of sensations,” “awareness of breathing,” “awareness of the present moment,” and “awareness of thoughts.” Once a solid foundation has been laid, one can then devote all one’s strength to Buddha-recitation, so as to attain one mind undisturbed in holding the name.

For a Chan practitioner, the Preliminary Practices section is also the foundation for contemplating the mind and practicing Chan. With this solid foundation, contemplating the mind and practicing Chan come naturally and smoothly.
